title: Gammon with Parsley Sauce
subtitle: Boiled gammon joint with a classic white parsley sauce
excerpt: A whole gammon joint simmered in stock with vegetables and spices, then served in slices with a thick parsley sauce. A traditional British dinner that is practical, economical, and provides good leftovers.

recipe.sourceNotes: Boiled gammon with a butter sauce is a British tradition that predates the now more familiar honey-glazed baked ham. Parsley sauce is a simple butter or béchamel-based sauce with chopped parsley, the traditional accompaniment to both gammon and fish in British cooking. It was particularly popular in the mid-twentieth century and remains a standard in traditional British households.

recipeTools.notes: Big enough to submerge the joint.

content.text: Soaking the gammon overnight in cold water reduces the salt considerably. If you skip this step the cooking liquid will be very salty and the meat itself may be too salty to eat. Change the soaking water once if you remember. The cooking liquid makes an excellent base for a pea and ham soup the next day, so do not throw it away.

Drain the soaked gammon and place in a large pot. Cover with fresh cold water. Add the onion, carrot, celery, bay leaves, and peppercorns. Bring to a boil, skim the surface, then reduce to a steady simmer. Cook for 20 minutes per 500 g, so approximately 1 hour for a 1.5 kg joint. The internal temperature should reach 70 C.
Remove the gammon and rest for 15 minutes. Reserve 200 ml of the cooking liquid.

Make the parsley sauce: melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Stir in the flour and cook for 2 minutes. Gradually whisk in the milk, then add the reserved cooking liquid. Stir until thick. Add the mustard if using and all the parsley. Season carefully with pepper; taste before adding salt as the cooking liquid will have seasoned it.
Peel off the rind from the gammon and slice the meat. Serve with the parsley sauce, mashed potato, and peas.
